title: Safety lane throttles and team handoff matrix — Jun 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working draft for the safety-lane (gradual throttling) procedure, the cross-team handoff matrix for a traffic-shift rollout, and an initial release-notes draft to go with the change. It covers:
- When to open the safety lane (pre-scheduled cutovers, emergency hotfix rollforwards).
- Throttle windows and increment steps (traffic percentage, duration, health checks).
- Hand-off responsibilities across SRE, Serving Runtime, Observability, and Product.
- Concrete rollback/abort gates and telemetry queries to evaluate gates.
- Communication templates for Slack + status page snippets.
Notes to self: keep the safety lane independent of canary names; reusable across models, routes, and region shards.

High-level summary (one-liner):
Apply a safety lane (tiered traffic throttle) with explicit health gates at 0%->10%->30%->60%->100% over a 90–120 minute window; abort and roll back automatically or manually if SLO or error thresholds are breached.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before opening safety lane):
- Owner assigned (primary + backup) and pagerable oncall available.
- Release PR merged and smoke-tests green in staging.
- Dedicated telemetry dashboard with the following panels:  p99 latency, errors per-minute, token throughput, memory pressure per-host, kv-cache hit-rate.
- Rollout Jira ticket created and linked to PR (JIRA-RELEASE-4321).
- Canary variant artifact pinned for the safety-lane.
- Escalation Slack channel created (e.g., #release-safety-RELEASE-4321).

Safety lane throttle sequence (recommended default):
- Phase 0 (preflight): 0% traffic to new variant. Duration: 15m. Goal: warm caches, perform low-load smoke checks.
- Phase 1: 10% traffic for 15m. Gates: errors <= 0.5/min (global), p95 latency < 600ms, memory < 80% per-host.
- Phase 2: 30% traffic for 20m. Gates: errors <= 1.5/min, p95 < 700ms, kv-cache hit-rate >= baseline-5%.
- Phase 3: 60% traffic for 20m. Gates: errors <= 4/min, p95 < 900ms, throttling events none.
- Phase 4: 100% traffic for 20m. Gates: final verification, no systemic regression signals.
If any gate fails during a phase: execute abort flow (see Abort & rollback).

Abort & rollback flow (quick checklist):
- Oncall posts brief incident message to Slack release channel (template below).
- Trigger automated rollforward-to-origin (route traffic back to previous model/variant).
- SRE collects diagnostics snapshot (last 30m logs, heapdump if applicable, host-level metrics).
- Serving runtime owner opens hotfix branch or pins previous artifact.
- Notify product + support and open a postmortem tracker (owner: release lead).
- If rollback unsuccessful within 15m, escalate to Eng Director & CTO on-call.

Automated abort triggers (examples — thresholds configurable per release):
- Errors per minute for new variant > X (configurable; default 5/min) sustained for 3 minutes.
- Increase in p95 latency > 30% vs baseline sustained for 5m.
- New 5xx types or unknown error classes detected.
- OOM or rapid host churn in the serving pool.
- Telemetry pipeline health (no events arriving) — do not continue until pipeline restored.

Telemetry queries (quick copies for dashboards / playbooks):
- Errors per minute (new-variant): sum(errors) by 1m where variant="new"
- p95 latency (route X): histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_bucket[5m]))
- KV cache hit-rate: sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_hits + kv_misses) by 5m
- Host restart events: count(host_restarts{pool="release-4321"})
- Token throughput: sum(tokens_generated) by 1m
(Notes: exact expressions depend on Grafana/Prometheus naming. Convert as needed.)

Team handoff matrix (roles + who does what during each phase):
- Release Lead (primary: Sofia Alvarez, backup: Marcus Chen): coordinates timeline, authorizes phase transitions, owns release Jira.
- Serving Runtime (oncall: Jordan Patel): monitors runtime metrics, executes variant pin/unpin, collects runtime traces.
- SRE (oncall: Ellen Park): monitors infra, executes route rollback, runs host-level forensics.
- Observability (owner: Ravi Kumar): checks telemetry pipelines, validates queries, ensures dashboard integrity.
- Product/Support liaison (TBD): prepares user-facing release notes, triages customer tickets.
Handoff checkpoints:
- 10m prior to Phase 1: Release Lead confirms all owners online.
- At each phase end: Release Lead solicits "GO/WAIT/ABORT" from SRE + Serving Runtime + Observability.
- On abort: SRE acts to remove new variant from router; Serving Runtime performs postmortem snapshot.

Detailed minute-level calendar (example for 90m window):
- T-30m: final preflight checklist; slack channel created; preflight smoke run.
- T-15m: open safety lane (Phase 0). Warm caches.
- T0: move to Phase 1 (10%).
- T+15m: evaluate gates, decision point -> Phase 2 (30%) or abort.
- T+35m: evaluate gates, decision point -> Phase 3 (60%) or abort.
- T+55m: evaluate gates, decision point -> Phase 4 (100%) or abort.
- T+75m: verification window; begin minor release-note publish + metrics snapshot.
- T+90m: close release, update Jira, remove temporary channels.
(Adjust times for 120m plan if extra conservative.)

Communication templates (Slack + status page)
- Slack: [release-safety-RELEASE-4321] Phase 1 -> 10% traffic applied. Monitoring: p95, errors, memory. Owners: @Sofia, @Jordan, @Ellen.
- If abort: [release-safety-RELEASE-4321] ABORTING: traffic reverted to previous variant. Cause: elevated 5xx. Postmortem-issue: JIRA-RELEASE-4321.
- Status page blurb (short): We are rolling out performance improvements to the inference routing layer. A staged rollout is underway. If you encounter degraded responses, contact support.

Draft release notes (to be trimmed for public):
- Title: Service routing overhaul: safety-lane rollout for lower-latency inference
- Summary: We rolled out a staged routing update that improves routing efficiency for the .generation API, reduces cold-start tail latency by leveraging improved KV cache warmup, and enables faster failover. The rollout used a safety-lane (tiered traffic) pattern and is now at 100% in selected regions.
- Impact: No user-facing breaking changes expected. Minor transient increases in latency possible during warmup.
- Rollout details: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 90 minutes.
- Known issues: We observed a small uptick in 5xx in one AZ (now rolled back automatically).
- Contact: support@redwood.ai (link to support ticket form)

Open questions / TODOs (explicit items we still need to resolve):
- Finalize exact numeric thresholds for errors/min for each class of release (hotfix vs feature).
- Determine who owns the public-facing release notes signoff (product or comms?).
- Add automated runbook steps to the routing controller for sub-15m automated rollback.
- Validate telemetry names and add them to the templated dashboard repository.

Artifacts to attach (placeholders):
- runtime change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987
- dashboard snapshot: confluence attached image (see linked artifacts)
- Jira: JIRA-RELEASE-4321

Immediate next steps (for the release lead):
1) Confirm owner roster and backups. (Sofia -> confirm by 2026-06-03)
2) Create release channel and populate pinned messages (release lead).
3) Push the dashboard snapshot to the release Jira.
4) Run a dry-run in staging using the exact safety-lane steps and record the timeline.

Appendix: short Slack message templates (copy/paste)
- Phase start: [release-safety-RELEASE-4321] STARTING Phase X: applying Y% traffic to variant "v123". Owners: @Sofia @Jordan @Ellen. Please watch p95/errors.
- Phase ok: [release-safety-RELEASE-4321] PHASE X OK: metrics look healthy. Moving to next phase in 1m.
- Phase abort: [release-safety-RELEASE-4321] ABORT: rolling back to previous variant. See JIRA-RELEASE-4321 for details.

End of draft. Please add comments inline or ping me in #release-planning if you have objections to default thresholds.
